Only two things call `RecordSelectorController`: the `recordSelector` LWC and the `RecordSelectorControllerTest` test class. No other Apex class references it.

I read the bodies of all 27 unmanaged Apex classes in `AgentforceOrg` and the four files of the `recordSelector` LWC bundle.

**Callers**

| Caller | How it uses the controller |
|---|---|
| `lwc/recordSelector/recordSelector.js` | It has three static imports: `@salesforce/apex/RecordSelectorController.searchRecords`, `.saveSelectedRecords` and `.getSelectedRecordsDetails`. |
| `RecordSelectorControllerTest` | It calls `searchRecords`, `saveSelectedRecords` and `getSelectedRecordsDetails` directly in 7 test methods. |

The other 24 classes are the Account, Case and Lead services, selectors, trigger handlers, batches, schedulers and their tests. None of them mention the controller. There are no Aura components in the org.

**What breaks if you rename it**
- **The LWC fails to deploy or compile.** The three imports use the class name in the path. Rename the class without editing them and `recordSelector` won't resolve its Apex imports. The component is exposed on record, app and home pages, so it would stop working wherever it's placed.
- **`RecordSelectorControllerTest` fails to compile.** It references the class by name in every test method, so a rename without updating it blocks deployment. With the test class broken, you'd lose the test coverage for the controller.
- **Nothing else in the org breaks.** Pages reference the component as `c:recordSelector`, not the Apex class, so they are unaffected.

**What I couldn't check**
- **Dynamic references:** `Type.forName('RecordSelectorController')` or a string-built call in some other class would also break. I saw none in the bodies I read.
- **Non-code references:** Profile and permission set `classAccesses` entries and flows aren't covered by my search. Profiles and permission sets that grant access to the class would need updating, and I'd check those in your local metadata or with a retrieve.
- **Renaming in place:** Apex classes can't be renamed in the org UI once deployed. In practice you'd deploy a new class and delete the old one.

**Suggested approach**
1. Rename the class and `RecordSelectorControllerTest` together.
2. Update the three LWC imports.
3. Deploy everything in one deployment, then run the tests.

I can make those edits and deploy if you want. Your local project at `C:\Users\ashis\sfb\runs\T5_A_org_173923\work` isn't a git repo, so I'd retrieve the source first.
